title: TIL - Choosing Between Code, an LLM Call, and an AI Agent
content:
Two questions sent me down this path. Question one: what is an "AI agent," really? Most job posts mention them. I had not looked into it deeply, and from the outside I could not tell what it referred to. Is an agent a different endpoint? A different model? A library we install? Or is it just a name for calling an LLM API in some particular way? Question two came later, and it stopped me cold. Once I understood the mechanics and sat down to pick something to build, I could not come up with a single idea that I could not also write as ordinary Go: a function that calls some APIs, hits a database, and returns a result. If plain code can do it, why pay a model to do it worse? This is what I found. There is a real answer to both, and the second one has a trap in it. So I built both Code: github.com/Arkoes07/llm One Go service, one interface, four endpoints of increasing complexity: POST /chat/no-memory        one stateless LLM call
POST /chat                  multi-turn, history per session
author: M. Alwi Sukra
summary_zh: 作者从「什么是 AI Agent」和「如果普通代码能做，为什么要花钱让模型做得更差」两个问题出发，用 Go 分别实现了普通代码版和 Agent 版做对比，梳理出何时该用确定性代码、何时用单次 LLM 调用、何时才真正需要 Agent 的判断标准。对于容易滥用 Agent 架构的开发者是一篇有价值的祛魅式思考。
